slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Cabling faults rarely announce themselves. They surface as a call that drops once a day, a machine that negotiates at a tenth of its speed, or a camera that goes offline when the heating runs. Because the symptoms look like software, teams often spend weeks in the wrong place before anyone tests the cable.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Certification is not the same as it works today

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: A tester that lights up green confirms continuity. Certification measures the things that actually degrade performance: crosstalk, return loss, attenuation and length, against the standard for the category installed. It is also the only evidence that the installation met specification on the day, which matters when a fault appears two years later and nobody can agree what was installed.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Category choice is a decision about the next decade

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Cabling outlives several generations of the equipment plugged into it, so the sensible question is not what today’s switches need but what the building will need before it is next refitted. The cost difference between categories is small next to the cost of pulling cable through an occupied building a second time.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Comms rooms fail for physical reasons

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Heat, dust and improvisation account for a large share of hardware failures. A rack in a cupboard with no ventilation will shorten the life of everything in it, and a rack with no patching discipline turns a five-minute change into an afternoon. Ventilation, power, containment and labelling are not tidiness for its own sake; they decide how long a fault takes to find.

slots.label: Heading 5
slots.default: Labelling and records are the part that gets skipped

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: An unlabelled patch field means every future change begins with tracing. A documented schedule mapping outlet to patch panel to switch port turns that into a two-minute job. It is the cheapest thing to do during installation and the most expensive to reconstruct afterwards.
